title: The Social Media Management Agent
description: Autonomous social content creation, scheduling, and engagement monitoring
prompt:
You are a social media management agent for my brand. Your job is to plan, create, optimize, and monitor social content — consistently, on-brand, and without needing my input on every post.

Brand context:
Brand name: [NAME]
What we do: [ONE SENTENCE]
Audience: [WHO FOLLOWS US AND WHY]
Brand voice (3 words): [e.g. "Expert, accessible, direct"]
Topics we post about: [LIST 4-5 CONTENT PILLARS]
Topics we NEVER post about: [e.g. "politics, competitors by name, anything unverified"]
Platforms: [e.g. "LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Instagram"]

Weekly content plan request:

Produce a 7-day content calendar with the following:
- 1 post per day per platform (or as specified)
- Mix of content types: original insight, curated resource, behind-the-scenes, engagement question, data/stat
- Each post should serve one of the content pillars
- No two consecutive posts should use the same format or content type

For each post:
PLATFORM: [which platform]
DAY/TIME: [suggested posting time based on platform best practices]
FORMAT: [text / image + caption / carousel / video script / thread]
CONTENT: [full ready-to-post copy]
HOOK ANALYSIS: [why the first line earns the scroll-stop]
CTA: [what you want them to do — like, reply, click, save]
HASHTAGS (if applicable): [3–5 specific, not generic]

After the 7-day plan:
WHAT TO WATCH: 3 engagement signals that would tell you the strategy is working.
WHAT TO STOP: 1 content type to retire based on what typically underperforms.
useCase: Autonomous social content creation, scheduling, and engagement monitoring
variables: e.g. "politics, competitors by name, anything unverified"
suggested posting time based on platform best practices
text / image + caption / carousel / video script / thread
why the first line earns the scroll-stop
what you want them to do — like, reply, click, save

title: The Content Repurposing Pipeline Agent
description: Automatically converting one long-form asset into a complete multi-platform content package
prompt:
You are a content repurposing agent. I am going to give you one piece of long-form content, and you will produce a full platform-native content package from it — maximizing reach without me having to create anything else from scratch.

Original content: [PASTE YOUR BLOG POST, PODCAST TRANSCRIPT, VIDEO SCRIPT, OR ARTICLE]
My brand voice: [3 adjectives describing how you communicate]
My active platforms: [LIST — e.g. "LinkedIn, Twitter/X, email newsletter, Instagram, YouTube Shorts"]

From the original content, produce:

1. LINKEDIN POST (native long-form):
Hook line (must earn the scroll-stop without reading further), 3-4 short paragraphs of insight, one question at the end to drive comments. Under 250 words. No hashtag spam.

2. TWITTER/X THREAD (10–12 tweets):
Tweet 1 is a standalone hook. Tweets 2–10 each make one specific point. Tweet 11 is the summary. Tweet 12 is the CTA. Every tweet under 280 chars.

3. EMAIL NEWSLETTER SECTION (200 words):
Feels like a personal letter. Written as insight-from-experience, not as content summary. One clear takeaway.

4. INSTAGRAM CAPTION (with visual direction):
Short punchy hook. 3–5 lines of value. CTA. Under 150 words. Plus: one-line visual direction for the image/reel that would accompany it.

5. YOUTUBE SHORTS / REELS SCRIPT (60 seconds):
Hook in first 3 seconds. Main point in 45 seconds. CTA in final 12 seconds. Written as spoken words, not prose.

6. PULL QUOTE (standalone image text):
One sentence from the content, rewritten if needed, that works as a standalone shareable image with no context.

7. FAQ SECTION (5 questions):
The 5 questions this content answers — formatted for a blog FAQ or website page.
useCase: Automatically converting one long-form asset into a complete multi-platform content package
variables: PASTE YOUR BLOG POST, PODCAST TRANSCRIPT, VIDEO SCRIPT, OR ARTICLE
LIST — e.g. "LinkedIn, Twitter/X, email newsletter, Instagram, YouTube Shorts"

title: The Content Repurpose Machine
description: Takes one long-form piece and extracts 8 different content formats ready to publish across different platforms
prompt:
Repurpose the following content into 8 different formats:

Original content: [original content]
My platforms: [platforms]
Brand tone: [brand tone]

Generate:
1. LinkedIn post (hook + value + CTA, under 200 words)
2. Twitter/X thread (opener + 5-7 tweets + closer)
3. Email newsletter intro (150 words, feels personal)
4. Instagram caption (punchy, with hashtag suggestions)
5. YouTube video script outline (sections + talking points)
6. Pull quote (one quotable line that works as a standalone image)
7. FAQ section (5 questions the content answers)
8. Short-form summary (3 bullet points for a busy person)

Rules:
- Each format must be platform-native — not the same text resized
- LinkedIn ≠ Twitter ≠ Email. Each has different norms.
- No format should require the reader to have seen the original
useCase: Multiplying the reach of every piece of content by extracting 8 platform-specific formats from a single long-form asset.

Instagram Strategy Framework:

The first prompt addresses foundational messaging. To prevent narrative dilution across a high-volume posting schedule, foundational brand messaging must be engineered before any individual asset is created. The first prompt establishes the semantic boundaries for all subsequent content. The prompt is structured as follows: "Act like a brand messaging coach. I am a [insert profession/niche]. I help [insert target audience]. They struggle with [top one or two operational/emotional problems]. My brand voice is strictly defined by these three adjectives: [adjective 1, adjective 2, adjective 3]. Write: one 12-word 'what I do' declarative line, a one-sentence optimized Instagram bio, and 10 Instagram post hooks written strictly in my voice." The strategic objective of this prompt is to eliminate generalized, verbose AI formatting and establish a reproducible, highly specific lexicon. The algorithmic value lies in the generation of hooks optimized for high initial retention, which is the critical metric for initiating carousel swipe-through rates.

Instagram Strategy Framework:

The second prompt focuses on architectural consistency. Inconsistency actively penalizes algorithmic standing, rendering ad-hoc posting strategies obsolete. This prompt generates a structurally sound architecture integrating Carousels, Reels, and Stories. The exact phrasing is: "Create a rigorous four-week Instagram content plan with three primary posts per week. My audience is [describe audience psychographics]. My primary offers/products are [list offers]. My operational goals are [sales, leads, visibility, traffic]. Each week must sequentially include: one multi-slide educational carousel, one short-form Reel, and one narrative Story sequence. For each post, explicitly detail: the core topic, the psychological hook, the specific call-to-action (CTA) optimizing for Saves or Sends, and a brief script for on-camera delivery." This prompt operationalizes the proven 2026 cadence of utilizing 3–5 carousels per week integrated with Trial Reels, ensuring a balanced distribution of top-of-funnel reach and bottom-of-funnel conversion assets.

Each caption must rigidly follow this structural flow: an opening counter-intuitive hook, a short relatable story or empirical proof point, a clear outline of what the user receives, and a low-friction call to action (e.g., 'Comment [Keyword] for the link'). The tone must remain [friendly, confident, conversational] and avoid hyperbole." The strategic objective is to utilize keyword triggers for automated DM responses, leveraging the 2026 emphasis on DM conversations as the primary signal the algorithm uses to determine relationship closeness.

This prompt functions as a universal refinement command to inject conversational authenticity. The directive is simple but powerful: "Rewrite the previous output. Make it 20% shorter, highly conversational, remove all complex adjectives, and embed one hyper-specific, relatable real-world example." This humanizes the text, directly counteracting the skepticism prevalent among Gen Z and Gen Alpha demographics, who possess highly tuned sensitivities to synthetic content. By forcing the AI to provide a specific example, the cognitive abstraction of the text is grounded in reality.

The tenth prompt in the organic video space utilizes the Zeigarnik effect through the "What Happens Next?" narrative cut-off. The creator posts a highly engaging video—often featuring something satisfying, precarious, or unusual—but abruptly cuts the video exactly one second before the climax or resolution. The caption prompts the audience: "Wrong answers only: What happens next?" or "Part 2 is in my stories." This psychological prompt forces the viewer into a state of cognitive dissonance, compelling them to comment their theories or navigate to the profile to seek resolution. The resulting profile visits and comment velocity aggressively signal content quality to the algorithm.Phase III: The "Add Yours" Participatory EcosystemThe introduction and global maturation of the "Add Yours" sticker fundamentally altered Instagram Stories from a broadcast medium to a collaborative thread medium. This sticker allows users to create public content threads, prompting followers to respond with their own stories, which are then aggregated. Tapping the sticker allows users to view everyone who has joined the chain, creating massive network cross-pollination and discoverability for smaller accounts.

Instagram Strategy Framework:

The fourteenth prompt utilizes the Screenshot Fill-in-the-Blank mechanic. This requires a two-slide story sequence. Slide 1 features a completed graphic template (e.g., "My 2026 Tech Stack," "My Morning Routine Matrix," or "Travel Bucket List"). Slide 2 presents the blank template with the "Add Yours" sticker superimposed, prompting: "Screenshot, fill it out, and Add Yours! 📝". The strategic brilliance of this prompt is physical interaction. It forces the user to press and hold the screen to freeze the story and take a screenshot, which drastically increases the "time-on-story" metric, before generating User Generated Content (UGC).
